Contact and Programming Information
DCCC offers a variety of nonclinical, CBT serviced, described below.
T4G: Thinking for Good
e Length: 14 weeks
* Cognitive Restructuring- Criminal Focus and Social Skills Development
e Moderate and High/Very High-Risk only
Workbook focuses especially on typical criminal thinking issues such as: Everyone lies, cheats, and
steals; no one can be trusted; the rules don’t apply to them; that all relationships are manipulative
MRT: Moral Reconation Therapy ©
e Length: 20 weeks
e Cognitive Restructuring
e Moderate and High/Very High Risk only
This program provides a method designed to promote positive self-image and identity; it helps
participants learn positive social behaviors and beliefs, and to begin to make their decisions from higher
levels of moral judgement. MRT is widely recognized as an Evidence-Based Practice by SAMHSA’s
National Registry of Evidence-based Programs (NREPP)
$Q: Staying Quit
* Length: 12 weeks
e Cognitive Restructuring
e Moderate and High/Very High-Risk only
Staying Quit helps clients avoid a relapse by recognizing risky situations, coping with urges and cravings,
being around users, understanding support issues, and taking charge. The materials help you
understand which situations and people may trigger a relapse. This enables you to target the riskiest
situations.
Coping with Anger- Men and Women
e Length: 12 weeks
e Cognitive Restructuring and Social Skills Development
e Moderate to High/Very High (Low Risk on a case by case basis)
1

--- Page 2 ---
Coping With Anger is targeted to adults who have problems with managing feelings of anger and
frustration in an appropriate way. It is used with those who are, argumentative or oppositional, as a
supplemental program with domestic violence perpetrators, with road rage, substance abuse, and drug
courts.
WAITLIST-Parenting and Family Values

e Length: 15 weeks

e Closed Class

e Cognitive Restructuring and Family Relationship Development

* All Levels
Parenting and Family Values is geared toward anyone who desires to become a better parent.
Participants are walked through the stages of personal development, from infancy through the teenage
years, and guided in an analysis of how they currently parent, what may be positive and negative about
their individual parenting style, and how it might be improved.
Untangling Relationships/Peer Relationships

e Length: 15 weeks

e Cognitive Restructuring and Relationship Development

* Alllevels
Untangling Relationships is designed to help those individuals who are either currently in or have a
history being involved in co-dependent relationships. Co-dependency and independency are explored,
including the benefits and the drawbacks of various types of relationships. Clients learn to identify the
"red flags" of unhealthy relationships, how to avoid them, and how to escape such relationships if they
are already in them.
WAITLIST- Taking Charge of My Finances

* Length: 5 weeks bi-monthly

® Closed class

* Money Skills Development

e $500 behind or more on fees, All Levels
The Taking Charge of My Finances Journal is designed to help provide information and helpful
techniques for making responsible financial decisions. Individuals will evaluate their current financial
circumstances, learn practical tips for managing their money and consider positive steps they can take
that will work for them now and in the future to take control of their finances.

2

--- Page 3 ---
MRT-Breaking the Chains of Trauma- Men and Women
o Length: 12 weeks
o Cognitive Restructuring
o Moderate to High/Very High (Low Risk on a case by case basis)
Breaking the Chains of Trauma is designed to be the beginning of the recovering from trauma
without asking the client to relive the traumatic experience. The program is designed to an
eight-session group format that can be implemented in an open-ended format (where new
participants can enter at any time). There are separate workbooks for male and female
participants and a Spanish version is available.
Seeking Safety — Men and Women
o Length: 24 weeks
o Cognitive Restructuring
o Moderate to High/Very High
Seeking Safety is an evidence-based, present-focused counseling model to help people
attain safety from trauma and/or addiction.
Thinking For Change — Men and Women
o Length: 15 weeks (meets twice weekly)
o Cognitive Restructuring
o Moderate to High/Very High
Drawing from cognitive restructuring theory, social skills development, and problem-solving
techniques, TAC offers a comprehensive approach to rehabilitation.
DCCC requires a variety of individual assessments as part of CBT programming, described below.
Assessments (CBT Programming)
e Texas Christian University- Criminal Thinking Scales
o The TCU CTS is administered to all participants engaging in CBT programming at DCCC.
The assessment is used to measure criminal thinking intervention effectiveness and is
given as a pretest when participants attend the DCCC Orientation and again as a post-
test when participants finish all of their required CBT classes.

topic_summaries.check_in: officer conducts a routine check-in verifying jerry's address at 1412 peyton avenue in indy, phone ending 96717, and confirms he still has the fencing company; check-ins are on wednesdays; in a later check-in there was no police contact over the last two weeks, jerry has two jail weekends remaining done every other weekend, still runs his company, and takes no prescription medications. Per Johnson County Community Corrections policy, check-ins should follow a set procedure: confirm address, phone number, and employment (with details if changed); confirm latest drug screen status; check ankle monitor and help resolve issues; check on medications and changes; review user fees; ask about police contact; confirm the schedule is entered for the following week; set the next follow-up meeting; and ask about the client's personal life.
topic_summaries.fees_payment: jerry owes $395 in fees and negotiates to pay about $300 now and the remainder in three weeks; in a later check-in his fee is $725 and marked done, with officer noting fees should be cut up by the 31st; at another point fees ran up to $1020 and jerry plans to pay half when paid after a payment wouldn't go through, keeping it current since he does incentive time; later jerry is actually paid in advance with an overpaid balance of $5,330 (about $1,330 to build through), so officer advises slowing payments to avoid slow county refunds; jail-day fees of about $300 will be reduced in bulk on the 11th after his final jail weekend since he can't be billed for jail time.
topic_summaries.property_taxes: jerry is stressed about $2000 in property taxes that increased this year, straining his electric bill; he later has his taxes paid and now must catch up on his gas and water bills due tomorrow.
topic_summaries.vehicle_purchase: jerry had a done deal on a 2021 denali yukon shipped to his house but backed out due to house taxes and his license situation; he confirms he no longer has the silver jeep cherokee, and later confirms no 2011 cherokee.
topic_summaries.economy: jerry is watching the market and economy, unsure whether it will go up or down, which factored into pausing a car purchase; he is worried about money because plumbing work is slow with nothing going on and slow work weeks putting him behind on fees.
topic_summaries.drug_screen: jerry reports easy sobriety, easier than expected, no thoughts, dreams, or urges to use or drink, only weird non-drinking dreams (used to smoke pot), and no prescription medications; he is not attending classes since already completed, and drug screens cost $15 each between now and august.
topic_summaries.ankle_monitor: jerry's ankle monitor is generally functioning and kept charged and confirmed still working good; on one occasion the control room called saying it was still in the orange after charging, going off at 3am, so officer suggests cleaning the metal port with a q-tip and will have tammy investigate; charging cuts in and out unless he sits very still, and officer again advises a dry q-tip on the magnetic charger/port, notes control can swap it, and gradual wear won't be billed though user damage would.
topic_summaries.work_plumbing: jerry runs his own fencing company working monday through saturday 7 to 6, staying busy; his son started working with him about a week ago; officer is glad he stays busy; on one occasion he took the last two days off over a nice weekend.
topic_summaries.appointments_scheduling: they switch from weekly to every-other-week check-ins scheduled two weeks at a time, next appointment pushed to the 21st at 6:30, with jerry emailing at the start of each week to set the off-week schedule; he meets his probation officer amber sijin today at 7 or 8; later the next check-in is the 4th at 6:30, the officer's email address changed and he's out until tuesday for a holiday weekend, wednesday program continues, friday daughter pickup and sunday dropoff are scheduled with extra travel time, and a doctor's appointment is coming end of june which jerry will keep the officer updated on to add to his schedule as it nears.
topic_summaries.community_service: officer will track 40 hours of community service with no rush and no penalty for waiting, likely started after jail time is done, aiming to finish before august when jerry's supervision ends; jerry wants it done so he can commit to regular saturdays.
topic_summaries.substance_evaluation: officer notes jerry is good on his substance abuse evaluation per kyle and has completed his impact panels; documentation will be forwarded/scanned to his probation officer amber sijin, and jerry should hand her a copy at his meeting. Dubois County Community Corrections (DCCC) offers nonclinical CBT programs relevant to substance issues, including Staying Quit (12-week relapse prevention), Coping with Anger (12-week, used with substance abuse and drug courts), MRT-Breaking the Chains of Trauma (12-week), and Seeking Safety (24-week evidence-based trauma/addiction counseling), all for Moderate and High/Very High-Risk clients. DCCC also requires assessments such as the TCU Criminal Thinking Scales, given as a pretest at orientation and a post-test at completion of CBT classes.
topic_summaries.incentive_time: jerry has incentive time to schedule, plans four hours tomorrow 6-10 at his girlfriend's, keeps six hours left, can do two hours sunday 6-8 to visit parents after getting out of jail (around 6); he must save and bring in receipts and cannot go to bars, clubs, strip clubs, or casinos; incentive time is otherwise flexible; he has up to 10 hours per week and plans a thursday 6-10 block (visiting/getting the bike out) and a sunday 11-5 block, avoiding places of common nuisance; a recurring sunday 11-5 block is set for every sunday given his 10 weekly hours, starting not this but next sunday, and is movable to a different day or time on request.
topic_summaries.location_monitoring: they review last week's locations which were everywhere for the job; girlfriend's address is 1502 murphy landing drive indianapolis 46207 and parents' at 5890 mcfarland; control room called noting robert again, and a field officer stopped by while jerry was 96 minutes late once; a recent week included a fort wayne trip to pick up his daughter needing extra drive time, and officer stresses obeying the speed limit and calling control when stuck in traffic to avoid a traffic stop and new charges.
topic_summaries.family_support: jerry reports family is doing okay, is waiting on his pass, his dad is not a phone person who won't return calls, and jerry has a good support system in place for the most part; family is getting older, no issues with friends or family, and he picked up his 12-year-old daughter from fort wayne.

substance_evaluation: Dubois County Community Corrections (DCCC) offers nonclinical CBT-serviced programs including Staying Quit (SQ), a 12-week cognitive restructuring program that helps clients avoid relapse by recognizing risky situations, coping with urges and cravings, being around users, understanding support issues, and taking charge, targeted at Moderate and High/Very High-Risk clients.

Coping with Anger (Men and Women) is a 12-week cognitive restructuring and social skills program used as a supplemental program with domestic violence perpetrators, road rage, substance abuse, and drug courts.

MRT-Breaking the Chains of Trauma (Men and Women) is a 12-week cognitive restructuring program for recovering from trauma without reliving the experience, available in male, female, and Spanish workbooks.
Seeking Safety (Men and Women) is a 24-week evidence-based, present-focused counseling model to help people attain safety from trauma and/or addiction.

DCCC requires individual assessments including the Texas Christian University Criminal Thinking Scales (TCU CTS), given as a pretest at DCCC Orientation and again as a post-test when participants finish all required CBT classes.
